item.title: Adieu la Chine : Google préparerait un changement historique pour l’avenir des smartphones Pixel

item.title: Pour les 200 ans de la photographie, Fujifilm installe sa Fujikina au Palais Brongniart [Sponso]
item.description: Pour célébrer les 200 ans de la photographie, Fujifilm prend ses quartiers au Palais Brongniart les 4, 5 et 6 septembre 2026. item.title: A new study says this breakfast staple can slow down how fast you age
item.description: Japanese researchers found that a daily serving of plain probiotic yogurt, combined with a healthier diet and moderate exercise, slowed biological aging in older men. A new study out of Japan, published in the journal Aging, found that biological aging slowed by 2.2% among a small group of older men who ate plain yogurt every day, in addition to adhering to standard recommendations for a healthier diet and moderate exercise....

item.title: 4 management lessons for scaling your team
item.description: When my company expanded from 10 to 90 people, I learned that more people meant more process. When my team consisted of 10 people, I could keep track of each team member’s tasks and their capacity. I understood the limits of people’s workload and even the circumstances that might affect their work. I hardly needed to delegate formally: if a task was difficult, I could redistribute the work myself, reinforce someone, or sit down and do part of the task with my own hands....

item.title: Career pathways are growing but evidence isn’t

Schools and states are responding by building new career pathways at a pace nobody would have predicted five years ago....

item.title: Creators now shape AI recommendations

In the past, search engines presented links for consumers to evaluate. Now, with the help of AI, answer engines interpret a question, assess the available evidence, and recommend a shortlist, sometimes even naming a single brand....

item.title: AI’s water problems run deep
item.description: The water footprint everyone’s tracking may only be a fraction of what AI’s growth actually costs communities and infrastructure. By now, most people understand AI requires enormous computing power and energy. U.S. data centers consumed about 183 TWh of electricity in 2024. That’s more than 4% of total U.S. electricity use in 2024, and demand is projected to more than double by 2030....
